# openobserve_synthetics (Data Source)

Lists the synthetic checks in an organization.

This is the fastest way to work out the `config` document a check type expects: build one in the UI, read it back here, and paste the result into `jsonencode()`. It also carries the server-assigned identifiers a `terraform import` needs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "openobserve_synthetics" "all" {}

# A check's identifier is server-assigned, so this is how to find what an
# import needs.
output "synthetic_ids" {
  value = { for s in data.openobserve_synthetics.all.synthetics : s.name => s.synthetic_id }
}

output "paused_checks" {
  value = [for s in data.openobserve_synthetics.all.synthetics : s.name if !s.enabled]
}

# The fastest way to work out the `config` document a check type expects: build
# one in the UI, read it back here, and paste the result into jsonencode().
output "browser_check_configs" {
  value = {
    for s in data.openobserve_synthetics.all.synthetics :
    s.name => s.config if s.type == "browser"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Data source ID, the organization identifier.
- `synthetics` (Attributes List) Every synthetic check in the organization. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--synthetics))

<a id="nestedatt--synthetics"></a>
### Nested Schema for `synthetics`

Read-Only:

- `config` (String) The type-specific settings document, as stored.
- `description` (String) What the check verifies.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the check runs.
- `folder_id` (String) Folder holding the check.
- `locations` (List of String) Where the check probes from.
- `name` (String) Check name.
- `synthetic_id` (String) Server-assigned identifier, which is what `terraform import` takes.
- `target` (String) What is probed.
- `type` (String) `http`, `tcp`, `tls`, `ssh`, or `browser`.
